The Brief in this order is a different object; never index _protocol with Brief keys. If a needed key is missing, raise an error that lists the available top-level keys instead of guessing a nested path.
[RL-0007] Define the feature columns once: every column of the frozen table except the targets, the excluded columns and the group column, and except key-like columns: text codes or integer sequences whose values are all distinct and carry no measurement. Continuous measurements are never identifiers, however many distinct values they have. Use exactly that list in every step, and never let a target or excluded column reach a fitted transformer or model.
[RL-0008] Before fitting preprocessing, screen the candidate features on training rows without fitting a model. Exclude, in the saved preprocessing, only features that are confirmed derivations of a target: exact equality with it, or a row sum of up to three non-negative columns that equals it on every training row. Features with absolute correlation of 0.98 or more with a target are a warning, not proof: keep them and print one line with their names. Print one line naming any excluded feature and the reason. Correlation warnings apply only to numeric outcomes; never coerce categorical labels to floats for Pearson correlation. Skip that numeric screen for categorical outcomes and retain exact-derivation checks.
[RL-0009] Keep feature names through preprocessing. When the encoded output has at most 300 columns, call set_output(transform='pandas') on ColumnTransformer and Pipeline objects and use OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', sparse_output=False). When it would be wider, keep sparse output inside one Pipeline that starts from the raw feature DataFrame, take names from get_feature_names_out(), and never pass that output to a transformer that selects columns by name. Use set_output only with components that support it; prefer built-in sklearn transformers with get_feature_names_out rather than custom components.
[RL-0010] Before encoding, sort feature columns into types: numeric; low-cardinality categorical (one-hot); text or code columns with more unique values than 5% of rows (drop, or use a frequency encoding fitted on training rows, never one-hot); date or time strings (parse with pandas.to_datetime, derive numeric parts such as hour, day of week and month, then drop the raw string). Integer 0/1 indicator columns stay numeric.
[RL-0012] Summary tables have one type per column: use NaN, not empty strings, for values that do not apply, or put numeric and categorical summaries in separate columns. Keep at most 50 rows and 12 columns; for wide summaries, place variables in rows and statistics in columns.
[RL-0013] Keep each script short and direct, about 120 lines or fewer: loop over columns instead of repeating blocks, no commented-out alternatives, no long docstrings, no restating of these instructions. A complete short script is better than an elaborate one that is cut off.
[RL-0014] When repairing, read the error type and message in the diagnostics first and change the smallest part of the script that causes it; keep the approach, inputs and outputs. A message about specifying columns with strings on non-dataframes means an array reached a name-based transformer (see RL-0009 and RL-0011). A KeyError on a JSON key means a guessed structure; use the keys the file has. Messages starting with 'MLCA:' state an engine rule; comply, do not work around it.
[RL-0015] When the training table has more than 100000 rows, avoid methods whose cost grows with the square of the row count (full silhouette, kernel SVMs, pairwise distances, t-SNE, agglomerative clustering) and prefer linear models with saga or SGD solvers, HistGradientBoosting or MiniBatchKMeans. Choose the cluster count only from internal criteria (silhouette, Davies-Bouldin, Calinski-Harabasz, stability). Scale features before distance-based methods. Deterministic table preparation may precede the split only through a declared prepared-data artifact. Later steps pass the declared source feature schema to the saved pipeline, never assume derived columns already exist in a freshly loaded partition. Inspect fitted input names; do not invent missing columns or fit replacement preprocessing during evaluation.
